families.name: actor-icon
families.definition: people, threads, processes, clients as small pictograms

families.name: bipartite-crossbar
families.definition: two aligned sets of cells/nodes joined by crossing lines or diagonal arrows: permutation networks, page/index remaps, crossbars, row-to-row mappings

families.name: brace-annotation
families.definition: curly braces, brackets, dimension lines grouping items with a label

families.name: check-cross
families.definition: ✓ ✗ ⚠ ⊘ stop signs, thumbs, "OK / FAIL" marks, in every style

families.name: clock-mark
families.definition: clock / timer / hourglass / tick-count glyphs

families.name: compare-marker
families.definition: good/bad, faster/slower, before/after marks that compare two panels

families.name: connector-style
families.definition: a distinctive connector idiom: colour+dash+head combination, orthogonal routing, bus lines

families.name: decision-diamond
families.definition: decision diamonds, yes/no branches, terminal pills, fork/join bars

families.name: delta-highlight
families.definition: how a changed element is marked: thick outline, glow, fill, hatch, colour, halo, star

families.name: formula-callout
families.definition: value bubbles, "= 42" boxes, small computation notes attached to a drawing

families.name: frame-arrow
families.definition: the arrow between frames/states (block arrows, "→ time", numbered transitions, big chevrons)

families.name: frame-border
families.definition: the border/box style used to delimit one state or panel of a sequence

families.name: ghost-copy
families.definition: the faded / dashed / grey copy of a previous state next to the new one

families.name: guarded-edge
families.definition: transition edges with guard/action labels, label boxes on edges

families.name: hash-bucket
families.definition: hash tables, buckets with chains, key→bucket arrows

families.name: hw-micro
families.definition: mux/demux trapezoids, registers, latches, gates, PE cells, bus-width slashes, crossbars

families.name: lane-divider
families.definition: swimlane dividers, lane headers, dashed separators between actors

families.name: legend-block
families.definition: legend swatch rows / key boxes when drawn in a reusable way

families.name: legend-row-swatch-label
families.definition: a legend drawn as rows of colour swatches each followed by its label

families.name: list-node
families.definition: linked-list nodes with next pointers, doubly linked, ring links

families.name: matrix-cells
families.definition: tables / matrices with values, highlighted cell, row/column headers

families.name: message-arrow
families.definition: sequence-diagram arrows between lanes (request/reply, dashed reply, lost message)

families.name: misc-icon
families.definition: any other pictogram (lock, key, disk, file, GPU, cloud, warning …)

families.name: packet-token
families.definition: packets, messages, tokens, tuples as small labelled boxes/circles moving along a path

families.name: panel-label
families.definition: "(a) before / (b) after" labels, panel title strips, step captions (only when drawn, not bare text)

families.name: pointer-cursor
families.definition: head/tail/cursor/index pointers into a slot; elbow arrows into a cell; null slashes

families.name: return-path
families.definition: dashed / curved / "back" arrows for loops, retries, replies

families.name: slot-array
families.definition: rows/columns of cells (queues, rings, bitmaps, buffers) with empty/filled/highlighted cells and "…"

families.name: stack-layers-gradient
families.definition: a stack of layers rendered with a gradient across the stack

families.name: stacked-cards-xn
families.definition: offset overlapping copies of the same card/frame (plus an ellipsis or xN) standing for many identical instances

families.name: state-node
families.definition: circle / rounded-rect state nodes incl. initial dot, accepting double circle, self-loops

families.name: step-arrow-label
families.definition: numbered or labelled arrows that carry the step marker on the arrow

families.name: step-badge
families.definition: circled / boxed / plain step numbers and letters, ①❶ⓐ (a) 1. — every font, fill and colour variant

families.name: strike-removed
families.definition: strike-through, cross-out, greyed-out, "deleted" marks

families.name: swap-move-arrow
families.definition: curved/double arrows that show an element moving or two elements swapping

families.name: time-span
families.definition: Gantt-like bars, waiting spans (hatched), overlapping intervals, event markers on a lane

families.name: timeline-axis
families.definition: time axis with ticks/labels, "time →" arrows

families.name: trace-path
families.definition: a coloured or thick path drawn over a grey/plain structure to show the route of one request

families.name: tree-dag
families.definition: tree / DAG node-link drawings: reduce and aggregation trees, hierarchies, layered dependency fans

families.name: tree-node
families.definition: tree / trie / B-tree nodes, parent-child edges, highlighted root-to-leaf path

families.name: zoom-callout
families.definition: magnifier wedges, dashed zoom regions, inset boxes with leader lines

families.name: access-badge-marker
families.definition: small role / permission / trust badges (R, W, padlock, checkmark, '?') attached to a field, slot or resource to say who may touch it

families.name: all-to-all-exchange
families.definition: every member exchanging with every other: NxN fanout triplets, dotted intra-group broadcasts, halo exchanges, replicated result rows

families.name: block-arrow-connector
families.definition: a thick hollow or solid block arrow used as the connector itself, often carrying a metric caption, a trigger label, or tapering/fading along its length

families.name: block-matrix-equation
families.definition: an arithmetic expression drawn as colour-coded block matrices and vectors with dimension labels, partitions and highlighted bands, instead of as a formula

families.name: call-return-arrow-pair
families.definition: a matched pair of oppositely-directed, differently-styled arrows between two components: call/return, acquire/release, trap/return

families.name: callout-arrow-label
families.definition: a curved or diagonal arrow pointing from an element to a bold annotation caption that names or argues about it (an annotation, not a step or data arrow)

families.name: capacity-topology-edge
families.definition: network-flow topology edges: double-parallel-line links labelled with capacity or flow/capacity fractions, counter-flow edge pairs

families.name: causal-mask-triangle
families.definition: a large right-triangle (causal attention mask) split into colour bands, shard zones or highlighted diagonals with callouts

families.name: cited-lemma-label
families.definition: a coloured proof/citation tag (e.g. 'Lemma F.2') attached to a diagram box or edge

families.name: cloud-shaped-logic-node
families.definition: a fluffy cloud / organic blob outline standing in for an unspecified block of logic, an opaque sub-circuit, a shared fabric or a shadow companion

families.name: cluster-oval-graph
families.definition: an oval (solid translucent or dashed) drawn around a small group of nodes or tokens to mark them as one cluster

families.name: colour-key-link
families.definition: colour itself used as the link: equation terms, assembled parts or taxonomy boxes tinted to match the component they refer to

families.name: composite-substate-container
families.definition: a state whose interior is itself a mini flowchart or a couple of named sub-states, drawn as one large panel nested in the outer diagram

families.name: concatenated-bitfield-row
families.definition: a bit-level register/address row assembled from several colour-coded named sub-fields, with per-bit digits, MSB tags and width labels

families.name: control-source-fanout
families.definition: a labelled source (controller, algorithm, request, selector) fanning out via elbow, dashed or comb arrows to the several things it drives or reaches

families.name: core-compute-row
families.definition: a labelled compute-unit row ('Core N: A x B = C') inside its own grouping container, operands colour-coded, often shown mid-accumulation

families.name: core-ring-rotate
families.definition: units arranged in a ring and linked by cyclic rotate / shift arrows that wrap from the last back to the first

families.name: cross-level-refinement-map
families.definition: two parallel chains or regions at different abstraction levels joined by dashed mapping arrows (refinement, simulation, phi / phi-inverse)

families.name: crossbar-transfer-arrows
families.definition: thick coloured block arrows carrying data between nodes through a shared fabric or cloud, crossing, merging or forming a transfer lattice

families.name: cycle-graph
families.definition: nodes closed into a directed cycle: deadlock circular waits, ring protocols, two-node mutual-dependency lenses, a slash marking the edge to break

families.name: cylinder-status-stack
families.definition: a database/storage cylinder icon whose interior or overlay carries state: labelled bars, partial fill, a refresh/retry loop

families.name: dashed-placeholder-slot
families.definition: a dashed-outline slot, box or panel standing for something not yet materialised: pending vs done, symbolic result, unknown operand, unshown continuation

families.name: delta-value-connector-arrow
families.definition: a connector between two sequential markers labelled with the computed delta or percentage change between them

families.name: dim-extent-array
families.definition: a grid or array of repeated units bracketed by double-headed dimension arrows naming the extent of each axis

families.name: document-icon-transform
families.definition: page / dog-eared note / tag icons used as objects: copied or converted document pairs, folded-corner spec boxes, bookmark tags

families.name: dual-style-arrow-relink
families.definition: one source with two differently-styled arrows to two targets, contrasting a stale link against the new active one

families.name: e-graph-numbered-eclass-box
families.definition: numbered dashed e-class boxes each holding e-node circles, with arrows from parent operators down to their operand classes

families.name: early-exit-ramp-cascade
families.definition: a main pipeline of stages where each stage also feeds a side 'ramp' that drains off a shrinking share of the work

families.name: edge-direction-arrow-pair
families.definition: direction arrows drawn beside a plain edge instead of recolouring it, including numbered opposing pairs marking a conflict

families.name: ellipsis-continuation-mark
families.definition: the mark that says 'this keeps going': dot ellipses, wavy squiggle breaks, off-frame repeat arrows, solid-to-dashed runs ending at an infinity glyph

families.name: equivalence-relation-mark
families.definition: a glyph or overlap asserting two things are the same: '=?' query marks, equivalence link arrows, hatched boxes whose shared region holds the equating formula

families.name: error-event-mark
families.definition: the mark for a failure event at a point: lightning bolts, jagged cracks, starburst explosions, exclamation ticks, zigzag break lines

families.name: extruded-3d-block
families.definition: a bar or slab drawn with distinct top/front/side faces (bevelled or isometric), used as a block or as one layer of a stack

families.name: fork-join-pipeline
families.definition: an input forking into parallel labelled branches that rejoin into one output, with an explicit fork node, wedge or merge hexagon

families.name: formula-defined-state-box
families.definition: a state-machine node identified by a multi-line logical predicate or formula instead of a short name

families.name: fractional-slice-square
families.definition: a square or cube resource icon divided by a line into a filled and an unfilled fraction, the split height carrying the meaning

families.name: function-box-state-update-oval
families.definition: a transfer-function box (title over a formula) dot-linked to an oval for a state update or a rectangle for a channel output

families.name: funnel-taper-connector
families.definition: a trapezoid/funnel shape that is itself the connector: it groups several things at its wide end and tapers into one target or span

families.name: geometry-sketch
families.definition: a small geometric sketch justifying a quantity: axes with slope lines and a rotation arrow, a plane with normal vectors and a dimension leader

families.name: gradient-fill-bar
families.definition: a bar or cell row whose fill is a smooth colour gradient rather than discrete categorical colours, reading as a continuous quantity or risk ramp

families.name: graph-rewrite-rule
families.definition: a before/after pair of small graphs joined by a chunky rewrite arrow, stating a rewrite rule rather than one figure's data

families.name: hatch-fill-encoding
families.definition: hatch/scribble fill used as an encoding: diagonal cross-hatch for skipped or invalid, different hatch patterns for different streams

families.name: highlighted-code-snippet
families.definition: a code / pseudocode / instruction listing panel, with tokens or lines highlighted, outlined or commented to point at what matters

families.name: highlighted-value-run-block
families.definition: an inline comma-separated run of similar values (not discrete cells) with highlighted contiguous sub-ranges, bracketed and labelled

families.name: hook-appended-node
families.definition: a structure grown by one element via a hook-shaped elbow or self-loop arrow from an existing node to the newly appended one

families.name: hub-leaf-fan-node
families.definition: a hub node fanning out to (or in from) many small leaves, including bundled bus ports and hub-and-ports router trees

families.name: icon-on-arrow
families.definition: a small pictogram (lock, gear, clock, turtle) sitting directly on a flow or link arrow, standing in for a text label or a status

families.name: inset-chart-panel
families.definition: a small real chart embedded inside a mechanism figure: sparkline, trend curve with an inflection callout, tolerance-band scatter, pie or dual-fill bar

families.name: isometric-cube-stack
families.definition: isometric 3-D cubes and cube stacks standing for tensors, devices or channel columns

families.name: labelled-container-with-badge
families.definition: an outer labelled box holding a nested, differently-coloured sub-panel, register or badge that carries the state

families.name: layered-bdd-node-diagram
families.definition: binary-decision-diagram circles arranged in dashed lane bands (one per decision variable) converging on a shared terminal

families.name: layered-relationship-overlay
families.definition: one set of nodes carrying two distinct relations at once, the second drawn as a thicker coloured overlay on top of the first

families.name: leader-line-annotation
families.definition: a thin leader line or dotted connector tying an offset label, margin note or detail box to the exact element it names

families.name: lookahead-preview-box
families.definition: a dashed grouping box holding shrunk miniature copies of upcoming or simulated states

families.name: lut-addr-val-box
families.definition: an Addr -> LUT -> Val lookup block: a bracketed row list fed by an index input and producing the selected value

families.name: memory-hierarchy-trapezoid-stack
families.definition: trapezoid storage-tier blocks stacked into a hierarchy and chained by bidirectional arrows to compute units

families.name: memory-region-segmented-bar
families.definition: a bar divided into labelled colour-coded regions of proportional width for a memory or resource layout, with boundaries, addresses and role swaps

families.name: motif-lasso
families.definition: a dashed freeform loop, blob, hatched polygon or wrapping band drawn around a cluster of elements to mark it as one motif or scope

families.name: multi-lane-step-bracket
families.definition: a dashed bracket-arrow beneath parallel lanes tying the simultaneous per-lane actions above it under one step caption

families.name: multi-level-pagewalk-chain
families.definition: a chain of small per-level index stacks, each with one highlighted entry, chained by arrows as a multi-level walk

families.name: necklace-arc-merge-highlight
families.definition: a row of touching numbered nodes on a band with connecting arcs above it, one arc recoloured to flag it rejected or chosen

families.name: nested-span-breakdown-box
families.definition: a span or operation box decomposed into internal named sub-phases sized by their share

families.name: nested-telescoping-bound-bars
families.definition: left-aligned bars of decreasing length nested inside each other, showing successive tighter bounds on a quantity

families.name: nn-layer-band-stack
families.definition: a stack of coloured bands, each a row of circle nodes, with crossing edges between adjacent bands - a small neural-net layer diagram

families.name: node-role-encoding
families.definition: node fill, outline style, shape or label used to encode a role or type (solid vs dashed, circle vs square, local vs remote, merged index set)

families.name: occupancy-fill-bar
families.definition: a bar or capsule partially filled to show a static occupancy or level, captioned or fed by an owner arrow

families.name: operator-symbol-chain
families.definition: explicit operator glyphs wired into a drawing: circled plus/multiply, bowtie joins, element-of links, ovals joined by plus signs, bare multiply badges

families.name: option-select-fork
families.definition: a set of candidate options of which one (or a checked subset) is picked, the rest greyed, the choice reached by a fork connector

families.name: organic-cut-boundary-curve
families.definition: a thick free-form curve or jagged cutout that threads between elements to mark a partition boundary or a selected region

families.name: orthogonal-feedback-loop
families.definition: a right-angle line that leaves a component, routes around and re-enters it (or an earlier stage) as a self-referential update loop

families.name: paired-boundary-anchor-markers
families.definition: a value framed by two matching start/end anchor markers so a reader can check both ends agree

families.name: parallel-arrow-bundle
families.definition: several parallel same-direction arrows drawn as a bundle, the count itself standing for N-way concurrency or relative frequency

families.name: param-list-operator-box
families.definition: a titled box or oval whose body is structured text: param=value lines, a state tuple, a rule, tensor metadata

families.name: pastel-function-block-pipeline
families.definition: a chain of pastel rounded function blocks / colour bands joined by hollow arrows, with coordinate-index labels tapping in and out

families.name: perspective-plane-panel
families.definition: a tilted foreshortened plane or wireframe frustum drawn in perspective, with projected content on or inside it

families.name: physical-device-schematic
families.definition: physical / materials device drawings: antenna split rings, layered sensor slabs, exploded assemblies, tunnelling gaps

families.name: pipe-capacity-packet-train
families.definition: a double-line tube between two nodes packed edge to edge with small packets, visualising a link's traffic against its capacity

families.name: port-square-node-box
families.definition: small square port nubs drawn on a box where each edge attaches, naming the interface as well as the link

families.name: priority-fallthrough-chain
families.definition: a vertical cascade of same-shaped tests where each false branch falls through to the next and each true branch exits to its own outcome

families.name: priority-queue-ladder
families.definition: a ranked vertical stack of open-ended queue lanes or entries, the classic multi-level-feedback-queue ladder

families.name: probability-split-arrows
families.definition: parallel arrows leaving one point labelled with complementary probabilities (p, 1-p)

families.name: promote-into-cache-curved-arrow
families.definition: a curved arrow feeding an item up into a tracked structure, showing it being promoted or admitted

families.name: protocol-header-stack-table
families.definition: a packet snapshot drawn as stacked protocol-header rows or a segmented header row, each field beside its concrete value

families.name: pruned-subtree-cutoff-bar
families.definition: tree edges converging onto a solid bar that caps them off, marking the subtree beneath as pruned or not explored

families.name: puzzle-piece-type-match
families.definition: facing edges cut as interlocking jigsaw notch-and-tab shapes: fitting cleanly means compatible, misaligned with a red X means incompatible

families.name: quantum-circuit-gates
families.definition: quantum-circuit notation: qubit wires, CNOT control/target glyphs, Hadamard and phase boxes, measurement meters, classical buses, ket labels, decoder blocks

families.name: queue-overflow-stack-tower
families.definition: a bracket or well standing above a full queue with the extra items balanced in it, showing work queued beyond capacity

families.name: radial-glow-blob-marker
families.definition: a soft-edged radial-gradient blob or ellipse with no hard outline, marking a point, footprint or region of interest

families.name: radial-merge-node
families.definition: several arrows from different sources converging on one node, cell, bar or point (fan-in), with or without a merge symbol

families.name: random-graph-icon
families.definition: a small generic node-link graph icon: an irregular scatter of nodes joined by edges, plain, directed, two-tone or with one node picked out

families.name: redrawn-variant-progression
families.definition: the same structure redrawn several times at a growing size, unroll factor or level, laid out side by side as a progression

families.name: region-partition-diagram
families.definition: a 2-D space carved into named regions or clusters - chords, quadrants, dashed cluster ovals, boundary curves, scattered labelled samples, search trajectories

families.name: ring-gauge-icon
families.definition: a ring, donut or circular-arrow glyph: segmented ring buffers, occupancy gauges, phase arcs, rotation and periodic-refresh loops

families.name: role-chain-boxes
families.definition: a short chain of differently-coloured labelled boxes joined by small arrows, showing one datum passing through named stages, tiers or roles

families.name: role-colored-node-mesh
families.definition: a small mesh of role-colour-coded nodes joined by several distinct edge types (one per link kind), often as a before/after pair

families.name: rotated-axis-arrow
families.definition: a long arrow carrying a sideways (rotated) text label naming the axis or the signal that crosses it

families.name: rotated-label-divider-box
families.definition: a narrow tall box or pill holding rotated 90-degree text, inserted inline to name a step, register or row group without widening the layout

families.name: sharded-tile-layout
families.definition: one rank's or machine's local shard drawn as a tile, cell row or card within the larger distributed layout it belongs to

families.name: skip-bypass-connector
families.definition: a line that leaves one point, bypasses the intermediate stages and rejoins further along: residual/skip paths, fault reroutes, detours

families.name: speculative-decode-token-tree
families.definition: a branching token tree with per-node probabilities and depth stages, colour-coded into accepted, drafted and unverified branches

families.name: speech-bubble-callout
families.definition: a rounded bubble, ribbon or thought cloud with a tail or prong, carrying a quote, intent, diagnosis, value snapshot or pseudocode block

families.name: stage-banner-band
families.definition: wide title / stage bands and chevron ribbons chained or stacked as the steps of a process

families.name: stat-summary-card
families.definition: a small card pairing a title with a stat, classification or summary line, drawn in plain and highlighted variants

families.name: subset-isolation-box
families.definition: a box, bracket or wedge drawn over part of a larger structure to isolate a subset, with a caption or ID naming what it represents

families.name: tagged-component-with-fields
families.definition: a component box holding internal field cells (value, metadata, owner, queue holder) plus an access-mode or state tag

families.name: task-schedule-lanes
families.definition: discrete colour-coded task tiles placed across parallel hardware lanes along a shared time axis

families.name: thread-squiggle-lane
families.definition: wavy squiggle lines standing for concurrent threads or process lanes, one recoloured or badged to mark it stuck

families.name: threshold-marker-line
families.definition: a labelled dashed cutoff line drawn across a structure or several stacked bars, marking a threshold or target value

families.name: tiered-role-frame
families.definition: a solid rounded container whose interior is divided into tinted, individually labelled role tiers

families.name: tile-shape-partition-grid
families.definition: a grid partitioned into equal or irregular tile groups to show the tiling shape, sometimes blank with one tile filled

families.name: tinted-component-box
families.definition: a plain component box whose fill treatment carries the meaning: gradient, saturated outcome fill, two-tone compartments, tinted sub-fields

families.name: titled-item-list-container
families.definition: a plain titled outer box holding a vertical stack of separate labelled items, often with an ellipsis gap or a bulleted rule list

families.name: torn-paper-edge-continuation
families.definition: a jagged or wavy torn-paper edge along a panel boundary, marking that the content continues or was cut off

families.name: waveform-signal-glyph
families.definition: wave and signal glyphs: sine bursts, antenna beam lobes, radiation fans, ECG squiggles, wave-textured propagation arrows, reflection stubs

families.name: token-strip
families.definition: A sequence drawn as a row, or stacked rows, of small token cells or chips coloured by role, modality, score or mask state, with brackets, arcs or lines showing grouping, alignment, attention or edits.

families.name: block-arrows
families.definition: Wide block arrows (hollow, filled or gradient-filled, sometimes holding a word) or large chevrons carry the hand-over between stages, panels or results, set apart from the thin arrows of data flow.

families.name: flow-type-arrows
families.definition: Arrow colour or line style tells kinds of flow apart - forward versus backward (gradient), training versus inference, clean versus unlabelled, main versus auxiliary, blocked gradients - explained by a key of sample arrows or by labels on the arrows.

families.name: embedding-space
families.definition: A sketch of an embedding, latent or feature space - a plane, blob or sphere with a few coloured points, clusters or thumbnails, decision regions or a boundary, and push, pull or movement arrows - showing what a module or an objective does to the representation.

families.name: colour-coded-groups
families.definition: One colour per group (view, client, task, modality, chunk) is kept on every element that belongs to it - inputs, intermediate blocks, outputs, legend rows, even the matching terms of a formula - so each group can be followed across the figure. The same device ties two distant elements that correspond - a claim and the panel that backs it, a prompt word and the mask it asks for, a graph region and the code lines written for it - by one shared colour in place of an arrow.

families.name: llm
families.definition: A large language model as a box, logo, robot or mascot.

families.name: dataset-card
families.definition: A card or stack of thumbnails with counts standing for a dataset.

families.name: prompt-box
families.definition: The prompt given to a model drawn as a text box, a card or a stack of text blocks whose slots or sections (task description, demonstrations, history, query, placeholders) are highlighted.

families.name: matrix-cell-grid
families.definition: A weight, similarity, score or mask matrix (or a stacked tensor) drawn as a small grid of cells whose fill pattern or colour carries the message - sparsity, pruning, low rank, sharing, masked patches, heat values - possibly joined by operator signs into a picture of a formula.

families.name: benchmark-card
families.definition: A question or task card with model answers, ticks and crosses.

families.name: chat-bubbles
families.definition: An exchange drawn as speech bubbles or turn boxes with speaker avatars, one per turn, tinted or outlined by speaker; several systems' answers may sit in columns aligned turn by turn.

families.name: gnn-graph
families.definition: A node-link graph: with message passing between nodes, as a small glyph standing for graph data, or as one worked problem instance.

families.name: vector-cells
families.definition: A feature, embedding or hidden vector drawn as a short row or column of cells, circles or bars, coloured by source, type or value.

families.name: zoom-callout
families.definition: Part of the figure is enlarged in an inset tied back to it by dashed leader lines, a cone or a magnifier: a block expanded into its internals (possibly over several levels), or a boxed image region magnified into a crop. The inset may also be tied to its source only by a shared colour and the repeated name, without a connector.

families.name: diffusion-chain
families.definition: A chain from noise to a clean sample with forward and reverse arrows; also a noise picture, a solver or denoiser box and the generated sample, or blobs of a noise and a data distribution joined by transport arrows (flow matching).

families.name: encoder-decoder
families.definition: Encoder and decoder as boxes or trapezoids narrowing towards a latent.

families.name: loss-gradient
families.definition: A loss drawn as a node with dashed or coloured arrows flowing back to what is trained, or as a double-headed arrow named by the loss between a prediction and its target.

families.name: schematic-plot
families.definition: A plot-shaped sketch with no measured data: named axes without ticks holding an illustrative curve, a 2x2 quadrant of regimes, methods placed at qualitative positions or regions, or a spectrum arrow whose poles name the extremes.

families.name: stacked-cards
families.definition: A dataset, batch or set of samples, tasks or languages drawn as an offset or fanned stack of overlapping cards, pages or frames instead of a single box. The same offset copies behind a module, head, layer or worker say 'several of these'.

families.name: transformer-block
families.definition: A block with attention and feed-forward sub-blocks, often stacked "xN".

families.name: attention
families.definition: Self- or cross-attention drawn as a block or as lines between tokens.

families.name: database-cylinder
families.definition: A dataset, corpus, memory or knowledge store drawn as a database cylinder (or a stack of them), named and sometimes sized, coloured by data type or split into parts.

families.name: notation-key
families.definition: A framed key inside the figure defines the paper's symbols or the operator glyphs (circled plus, times, concat, softmax) so the drawing itself can be labelled with bare symbols.

families.name: operator-nodes
families.definition: Small circles on the arrows carry an operator - plus, times, element-wise product, concatenation, sigma, a letter - where signals are summed, multiplied, gated or reduced.

families.name: verdict-marks
families.definition: Whole outputs, lanes, candidates or claims carry a verdict: a check or cross, thumbs, a happy or sad face, a short verdict word, or a red versus green tint of the lane.

families.name: agent-loop
families.definition: Observe / think / act (or plan / act / reflect) as a cycle around an agent.

families.name: masked-input
families.definition: Part of an image, spectrogram, patch grid or sequence is covered by grey, black or hatched blocks to mark what is masked, to be predicted, generated or edited.

families.name: option-catalog
families.definition: Each stage, decision or factor is drawn as a menu of options (chips, cards, option columns, decision nodes) rather than one chosen component, mapping a design space or the axes a study varies.

families.name: brace-grouping
families.definition: Curly braces, square brackets or tall parentheses gather several items - stacked prompt blocks, a run of thumbnails, a span of text, the inputs of a model - and name the group or hand it on as one arrow.

families.name: equation-boxes
families.definition: Stages or blocks are stated by their equations: boxes whose content is a formula, or a formula printed beside or in a callout from each block, lane or column, so the method reads as a derivation. Bare symbols or tensor shapes printed beside every module or signal, tying the drawing to the method's equations, are the light form of it.

families.name: highlighted-text-spans
families.definition: Spans inside sample text (prompts, answers, captions, reasoning, documents) are coloured, shaded or underlined to mark categories, evidence, key words, edits or errors.

families.name: module-state-coding
families.definition: Module states - frozen versus trainable, active versus idle, quantised versus full precision, optional versus base - are coded by fill colour, greying, hatching or dashed outlines with a key, including the same blocks redrawn once per phase or variant with the state changing. Removed, pruned or switched-off elements left in place as faded ghosts are the same device.

families.name: loop-back-arrow
families.definition: Iteration or feedback is drawn as one long return arrow from a late stage or the output back to an early stage or the input, usually around the outside of the figure and labelled with the round, the condition or the signal fed back.

families.name: pictogram-chain
families.definition: Pictograms carry the statement instead of labelled boxes: a chain of captioned icons for the stages, or icons joined by plus and equals signs (possibly with counts) that state the method as an equation.

families.name: typed-trace-blocks
families.definition: An LLM or agent run drawn as an ordered sequence of typed blocks - think, plan, tool call with arguments, tool response, answer - each tagged by type, in a lane, a numbered call list or a thought bubble, possibly forking into parallel threads.

families.name: contrastive-pair
families.definition: Positive pairs pulled together, negatives pushed apart, or a similarity matrix.

families.name: dual-encoder
families.definition: Two encoders drawn in parallel - one per modality, view or tower, sometimes sharing weights - whose outputs meet in a similarity, alignment or contrastive block.

families.name: frame-border-titles
families.definition: A frame's title is set into a gap of its border line, like a fieldset legend, instead of sitting inside or above the frame.

families.name: memory-store
families.definition: A titled storage box of past items (feedback, exemplars, knowledge entries) tied to an LLM or agent by paired retrieve and update arrows.

families.name: pill-title-headers
families.definition: Panels, cards or zones are headed by a filled pill, chip or band that carries the title (often with the panel letter), usually in the panel's own colour.

families.name: positive-negative-pairs
families.definition: Positive and negative samples (anchor / positive / negative, chosen / rejected, win / lose, A versus B) are drawn as colour-coded pairs and carried into the loss or verdict that pulls them together or pushes them apart.

families.name: small-multiples
families.definition: A row or grid of identical small panels - thumbnails, plots or graphs - that differ in one factor (step, noise level, time, strength, topology, case or method), so the eye compares along the row or down the column.

families.name: toy-values-inline
families.definition: Concrete toy values - small numbers in matrix cells, bit strings, probabilities, a mini data table with missing cells - are written into the method's own boxes so an operation can be followed by hand.

families.name: trapezoid-module
families.definition: A network, encoder, tokenizer or compressor drawn as a trapezoid (or a funnel) that narrows in the flow direction, saying 'this maps many to few' without opening the module.

families.name: accent-on-ours
families.definition: The proposed part is drawn in a saturated accent while the prior method, the baseline or the existing parts stay grey, pale or black and white - in the diagram or in the result bars.

families.name: annotated-record-card
families.definition: One dataset or benchmark record drawn in full with its labelled fields - the sample, its prompt or question, labels, evidence, metadata, verdict - to show what an entry contains.

families.name: code-snippet-box
families.definition: A monospace listing of real code, JSON or test code drawn as a box, card or editor window and treated as data - generated programs, code samples, diffs passed between stages.

families.name: cycle-ring
families.definition: A loop drawn as a closed ring: arrow segments, chevrons or icons around a centre (an agent, a mascot, a miniature of the system), one per step or role, read clockwise.

families.name: filmstrip
families.definition: Video drawn as a film strip: a row of consecutive frames, possibly inside a sprocket-hole border, one row per prompt, method or clip.

families.name: gridworld-map
families.definition: An environment drawn top-down as a floor plan, maze or grid world: walls, doorways, start and goal cells, objects as glyphs, sometimes a route or camera cones.

families.name: mlp-head
families.definition: A small MLP, linear layer or projection head.

families.name: search-tree
families.definition: A tree of candidate states, thoughts or token sequences expanded by a search (MCTS, beam search, tree of thoughts), with scores or values at nodes, possibly redrawn once per search phase.

families.name: tab-titled-panels
families.definition: A panel, card or block carries its title, letter or number on a small tab attached to a corner or edge of its frame, like a file-folder tab.

families.name: teacher-student
families.definition: Two models drawn as teacher (expert, EMA copy) and student, linked by distillation, consistency or EMA arrows, with the teacher supplying targets or pseudo-labels.

families.name: thought-bubble
families.definition: A cloud-shaped bubble trailing small circles to an agent, user or model holds what it thinks, imagines, intends or remembers: the typed outputs of a step, an imagined exchange, pictograms of intent, a gloss of what codes mean.

families.name: vae-codebook
families.definition: Encoder, latent or discrete codebook, decoder.

families.name: cnn-stack
families.definition: Convolutional layers as slabs or a pyramid of feature maps.

families.name: distribution-glyph
families.definition: A small bell curve, peak or bar histogram attached to a model output, token or loss arrow to show the distribution being matched, reshaped or compared.

families.name: error-callouts
families.definition: The wrong part of an output is marked in place: a red dashed box or circle on an image region, a red-tinted span or step inside an answer, or a short tag naming the error pinned beside it.

families.name: frozen-trainable
families.definition: Snowflake / fire, padlock or a colour key on modules.

families.name: lora-adapter
families.definition: A frozen weight block with a low-rank side branch (A, B) added to it, or an adapter module slotted into a frozen stack; the update drawn as small matrices joined to the pretrained weight by a plus sign.

families.name: retrieval-store
families.definition: A query going to a database cylinder or index and coming back with items.

families.name: rl-loop
families.definition: Agent and environment exchanging action, state and reward.

families.name: skip-connection
families.definition: A residual or skip path drawn as a line that leaves before a block, arches around it and rejoins after it, usually in a circled plus; also layer skipping or looping drawn as arcs over a row of layers.

families.name: vit-patchify
families.definition: An image cut into a grid of patches that become tokens.

families.name: attention-mask-grid
families.definition: Who attends to whom, drawn as a token-by-token grid of filled cells (causal triangle, blocks, bands, evicted cells, measured attention weights) or as fans of lines between two token rows.

families.name: before-after-pair
families.definition: One item drawn twice, before and after an edit or treatment - an image tile, a text answer, a matrix, a record, a network - side by side or stacked and joined by an arrow that names the change.

families.name: claim-banner
families.definition: A strip, pill or panel heading inside the figure states a full sentence - the headline claim, a per-panel takeaway, a research question or a plain caption of what to notice - instead of a component label. Panel titles that are short selling points (Large Scale, High-Quality, Diverse) rather than component names count as well.

families.name: layer-probe-taps
families.definition: Readout taps on a drawn model - probe glyphs or arrows from several layers to a linear probe, LM head or logit lens - showing where internal states are read.

families.name: level-ladder
families.definition: Ordered capability or difficulty levels (L0-L5, Bloom-style) drawn as a ladder, staircase or stacked pyramid of tiers, each tier extended with tasks, models or scores.

families.name: picture-overlays
families.definition: Vector marks are drawn on top of a photo, render, map or screenshot to show what the method sees or does there: boxes and masks, paths and arrows, axes, cursor traces, coverage regions, labels.

families.name: plot-callouts
families.definition: Measured plots carry drawn annotations that state the finding: shaded regime bands, dashed highlight boxes, bold take-away words, gain arrows.

families.name: pseudocode-box
families.definition: An algorithm, pseudocode or API listing placed inside the figure that states the method (or how to call the library) in code or numbered steps, beside or linked to the drawn parts.

families.name: radar-chart
families.definition: A radar (spider) or radial bar chart of per-benchmark or per-dimension scores, one polygon per method, embedded in an overview, teaser or agent figure.

families.name: rotated-labels
families.definition: Titles or names are written rotated by 90 degrees (or as stacked letters): band titles along the left edge, names inside tall narrow module boxes.

families.name: step-notes
families.definition: The steps or stages are narrated in words outside the drawing: numbered caption boxes beside it, a caption strip along the bottom with one 'Step N' note per column, or bullet lists beside each stage.

families.name: sunburst-taxonomy
families.definition: A ring chart of categories: a donut of shares or a two- to four-ring sunburst running from top-level groups to leaf tasks, with labels rotated along the sectors and often a logo or name in the hole; the coverage picture of a benchmark or dataset.

families.name: taxonomy-tree
families.definition: A hierarchy of categories, criteria, tasks or design choices drawn as a tree - a root, branch boxes and leaf boxes or thumbnails - or nested by curly braces.

families.name: audio-waveform
families.definition: Audio drawn as a waveform strip (sometimes turned upright as centred bars) standing for speech or a sound track, next to or under the frames, tokens or spectrogram it belongs to.

families.name: comparison-table
families.definition: A ruled table comparing methods or examples row by row against named columns - capabilities, criteria, formulas - with check and cross marks, numbers or small drawings in the cells.

families.name: cost-badges
families.definition: Costs or scores are drawn on each lane, design or output - run time with a clock, FLOPs or step counts, memory, coin stacks for budget, rows of icons as scores, a metric pill or a number printed on each render, a small metrics table or bar chart beside each schematic - so efficiency or quality is part of the comparison.

families.name: federated-round
families.definition: A server and clients exchanging model updates.

families.name: icon-led-titles
families.definition: Every box, card or panel title carries a small icon that names its concept, so the boxes read as captioned pictograms.

families.name: leader-callouts
families.definition: Labels, notes or whole cards are tied to the exact spot of a picture, chart or drawing they speak about by thin leader lines, often in the card's own colour.

families.name: margin-row-labels
families.definition: Row labels in the left margin name aligned rows that run across several columns, panels or cases, so the figure reads as a matrix of rows by columns.

families.name: multi-agent
families.definition: Several agents as avatars wired by message arrows or a topology.

families.name: neuron-network
families.definition: A neural network drawn as columns of circular neurons joined by lines (all-to-all or sparse), often shrunk to a small glyph that stands for 'a model'.

families.name: new:dashed-group-boxes
families.definition: a set partitioned into groups drawn as dashed-border boxes, each tagged Group k and holding a row of item icons plus dots, the boxes stacked with vertical dots inside one solid frame and named by a set equation underneath; used by acl25-002

families.name: state-snapshots
families.definition: The same object - a graph, list, table, matrix, token row or rendered scene - is redrawn after each step at the same scale, with only what changed recoloured, added or faded, so the procedure can be followed by eye.

families.name: task-definition
families.definition: The figure, or a strip of it, states the task rather than the method: example inputs and the desired or produced outputs, the learning setting or data split, with the model absent or drawn as one black box.

families.name: tool-use
families.definition: An agent calling tools, APIs or other models, drawn as icons around it.

families.name: vlm
families.definition: A vision-language model: image and text encoders feeding a language model.

families.name: attention-map
families.definition: An attention pattern shown as a heat map over an image or as a token-by-token grid; the two drawn forms are the parts saliency-heatmap and attention-mask-grid.

families.name: brand-logo-icon
families.definition: A real company, product, model or database logo (OpenAI, Llama, Gemini, GitHub, Wikipedia, ClinVar) used as the icon or node for a model, tool or data source.

families.name: camera-frustums
families.definition: Cameras or views drawn in the scene: frustum pyramids along a camera path, view thumbnails tied to an object by rays, translucent cones or polygons for what each view covers.

families.name: chain-of-thought
families.definition: Step-by-step reasoning drawn as a chain: Input, Thought, Thought, ..., Output boxes joined by arrows, the thoughts being text (or pictures), or a block of placeholder reasoning lines before the answer.

families.name: checkpoint-chain
families.definition: Successive model checkpoints (theta0 to thetaT, first to final reference model) drawn as a chain along one edge, with the data or data split that feeds each hop.

families.name: gui-screen
families.definition: A desktop, browser or phone screen - a real screenshot or a drawn mock window - that serves as the environment an agent observes and acts on, or as a gallery of tool interfaces.

families.name: human-in-loop
families.definition: A person is drawn as an actor inside the workflow who inspects, corrects, approves, labels or gives feedback on an intermediate result, not only as the source of the input.

families.name: illustration-style
families.definition: The drawing departs from flat vector boxes: isometric pseudo-3D cubes and slabs, hand-sketched strokes, painterly or 3D-rendered (possibly AI-generated) scenes, or pixel-art sprites.

families.name: knowledge-graph
families.definition: A knowledge, commonsense or scene graph drawn as entity or object nodes joined by edges that carry relation names; also single (head, relation, tail) triples.

families.name: leaderboard-table
families.definition: A ranked table of models with scores: rank badges or medals for the top rows, a logo or icon per model, bars or arrows for score and rank change.

families.name: method-timeline
families.definition: A dated axis with prior methods and the proposed one hung along it, grouped by family, placing the work in a line of research.

families.name: model-pictogram
families.definition: A model is drawn as a stock pictogram - a cartoon robot head that can show a mood, or a small node-and-edge network glyph - instead of a labelled box, a vendor logo or a named mascot.

families.name: new:fork-arrows-from-one-input
families.definition: one input (a picture slot with a caption) with two thin curved arrows leaving it, one bending up and one down, to feed two parallel branches of the figure (two encoders, two views, two baselines). Used by: iclr25-0101_fig1. Reusable as the

families.name: new:operation-pill-on-arrow
families.definition: a small pill-shaped label naming an operation or module (here MGL) sits on a connector that swings in one long curve from the block above to the block below, so the operation reads as something applied along the arrow instead of a box in th

families.name: schedule-lanes
families.definition: Lanes per device, worker, pipeline stage, request or session along a time or step axis, holding coloured work blocks, memory bars, idle or padded gaps and transfers - the Gantt-style schedule of systems and efficiency figures. Coloured bars along a time axis that give the span of each event under a film strip belong here too.

families.name: status-badges
families.definition: Small badges pinned to the edge or corner of a block, card or icon mark its status or where something applies: New / Optional pills, a tool icon on the components a method changes, an 'improved' badge on a retrained model, a circled abbreviation defined in the legend.

families.name: unet
families.definition: The U-shaped encoder-decoder with skip connections.

families.name: visual-metaphor
families.definition: The method or its parts are told through a drawn analogue - an everyday object or scene (a prism, gold mining, a river confluence, a character rolling down a loss curve) or the biological structure the model mimics - beside or instead of literal boxes.

families.name: condition-insets
families.definition: Each generated output is shown with the condition that produced it: a small glyph or inset (orientation cube, layout boxes, pose, sketch) on the output, or spans of a strip marked as condition versus generated.

families.name: judge-evaluator
families.definition: The evaluator - an LLM judge, a human expert, an auditor or a reward that compares outcomes - drawn with courtroom props: a gavel, a judge's robe, a balance scale.

families.name: mirrored-layout
families.definition: Two halves of the figure are drawn as mirror images - two branches, modalities, lanes or loops - with matching parts at matching positions and the links between them at the centre.

families.name: new:candidate-list-card
families.definition: a rounded grey card listing several candidate outputs (N-best hypotheses, beam results, sampled answers) as short lines with a closing ellipsis, amber highlight bars marking the words that differ or err, and a bold-italic title above the ca

families.name: new:captioned-picture-frame
families.definition: a rounded frame, usually heavy or tinted, that holds one sample picture (greyed as a placeholder) with its caption set inside or under it; the frame and caption are the part, the picture is left out. Used in cvpr26-0003_fig1 (teaser tile of

families.name: new:formula-as-tree
families.definition: an equation or operator expression drawn as a small tree: operand boxes (vectors as boxes of circles, a matrix as a small circle grid) feed circled sum or operator nodes, symbols (w, W, o) written beside the nodes so the drawing doubles as

families.name: new:labelled-pie-chart
families.definition: a small pie in two or three blues with the percentage and count written inside each slice (icons may sit in the slices). Used by: neurips24-0101_fig1

families.name: new:shared-model-sink-box
families.definition: a plain Model box (or a single model icon) that receives arrows from several workers, stages or prompts, with a short note or labels on the arrows saying what they mean (all workers update the same model; two prompts, one judge). Used by: c

families.name: point-cloud
families.definition: A 3D point cloud, mesh or Gaussian-splat render.

families.name: prediction-vs-data
families.definition: A theoretical or model-predicted curve or pattern is placed beside measured data on matching axes, so the reader checks that they agree.

families.name: problem-only
families.definition: The figure shows only the problem - limitations or failure modes of existing methods, a shortcut, a degradation or a hard case staged on concrete examples - and does not draw the remedy.

families.name: size-as-value
families.definition: The size of a repeated glyph or card carries a quantity: the same icon at growing sizes for model strength or cost, circles shrinking with a count, cards growing taller with difficulty.

families.name: spanning-shared-block
families.definition: A module, model or option that serves several columns, cards, stages or phases is drawn once as a bar or band spanning all of them, instead of being repeated in each.

families.name: support-query-sets
families.definition: A few-shot episode drawn as a support set (a few labelled samples) and a query set (one or two samples) entering the same model, which answers for the query.

families.name: embedding-scatter-plot
families.definition: Measured 2-D projections (t-SNE, UMAP, PCA) of learned features, coloured by class or domain, one panel per method or branch for comparison.

families.name: loss-landscape
families.definition: An objective drawn as a surface or as contour lines - a 3D bowl, hills and valleys, a tilted plane - with a descent path or one trajectory per method from a shared start.

families.name: mascot-character
families.definition: A cartoon character - an animal, creature, figure or characterful robot, possibly the paper's named system - personifies a model, agent or role, is reused across panels and may change expression or props.

families.name: new:accept-discard-bars
families.definition: one horizontal pale-blue accept bar and red discard bar per category, names at the left, a tick and cross legend above

families.name: new:adaptive-path-from-initial-point
families.definition: a search drawn as one dotted path that advances from an open initial circle to the target, captioned as adaptive. Used by cvpr25-0086_fig1 (panel e) as the contrast partner of the trial star

families.name: new:candidate-path-block-stack
families.definition: a vertical stack of named blocks (Input, Block 1..n, activation, Output) joined by down arrows, with dashed coloured arcs hopping over non-adjacent blocks to mark candidate connections of a search space or weight-shared supernet; a pruned c

families.name: new:candidate-selector-unit
families.definition: a selection module (white box, orange outline) fed from below by a dashed row of candidate tokens and returning a selected row above it, with a grey start token feeding it from the left and the selected row chained on to the next selector.

families.name: new:candidate-tile-concat-module
families.definition: a set of candidate outputs drawn as a dashed grid of small tiles inside a tinted titled region, assembled by a Concat box at the bottom after a search pill (Beam Search) at the top. Used by aaai25-0072_fig1 (Concator). Reusable for any stag

families.name: new:chain-rows-with-ellipsis
families.definition: alternative chains of different lengths stacked as labelled rows (PC1, PC2, PCn) of tiles and module boxes, with three-dot ellipses for omitted steps and a vertical ellipsis for omitted rows, inside one rounded box. Used by: aaai25-0067_fig

families.name: new:chevron-banner-labels
families.definition: long outlined chevron (pentagon-arrow) banners carrying a task, episode or stage name, set in a row with an ellipsis to stand for a sequence of tasks seen earlier (here Task 1 ... Task n above stacks of photos). Used by icml24-0110_fig1. Re

families.name: new:cls-binary-head
families.definition: two-cell column under a red heading: CLS token over its binary label

families.name: new:code-skeleton-bars
families.definition: blue-outlined card whose code lines are grey rounded bars with a few coloured bars and two dash-dot slots

families.name: new:corner-sample-thumbnail
families.definition: a small real photo (a node image, a sample, a screenshot) pinned over a corner of a labelled box so the box shows the sample behind it; one pin per box, same corner each time. Used by: cvpr26-0071_fig1 (photo over the upper right of each in

families.name: new:crescent-refinement-arrows
families.definition: three thick dark-teal crescent arrows stacked down a column on each side of a centre, each curling back against the flow with an arrowhead, joined by curly brackets to one agent or model in the middle; the two sides mirror each other. Figur

families.name: new:crossed-feed-wiring
families.definition: two (or more) source boxes each wired to every one of two target boxes by crossing straight lines with dots at the joints, the targets then merged by a bracket line into the next stage; reads as "each input goes through both operations". Us

families.name: new:dashed-capsule-regulariser
families.definition: a dashed purple capsule (or funnel) that a regularised path passes through, with arrows fanning out of its face towards the target and a purple arrow down from its foot. Figures: icml26-0036_fig1 (Strategy 1, Implicit Representation Alignme

families.name: new:dashed-colour-data-columns
families.definition: a set of items drawn as a narrow column of tiles, each with its own dashed outline in the colour of its kind of data, with an ellipsis in the gap. Used by aaai25-0072_fig1 (Output (Ad), (PV), (PVX), (P), one colour per kind). Reusable for o

families.name: new:dimension-lines-on-picture
families.definition: thin dimension lines with size labels (448) run along the top and left edges of an input image, the left label rotated, with the caption centred under the picture; used by iclr26-0034_fig1 for the high-res and the low-res image. Reusable fo

families.name: new:enhancer-promoter-arcs
families.definition: several enhancers (or other sites) joined to one target site (a TSS, a hub) by dashed arcs over a linear strand, with a promoter bar and distance labels. Used by iclr26-0025_fig1 (panel a). Reusable for any many-to-one link drawn as dashed

families.name: new:faded-item-stream
families.definition: dash-dot arrow carrying a sequence of items with the current item bold and the earlier and later items greyed, a box on the stream

families.name: new:forward-back-model-pair
families.definition: two model boxes side by side between a pair of data boxes (text above, units below): the left model carries an arrow up from the lower data to the upper data, the right model an arrow down the other way, so one picture says "A to B and back

families.name: new:generate-score-select
families.definition: one state fans out into several candidate rows, a shared checker scores each, the scores are compared in bars, and the winner is marked and carried on. Used by icml24-0072_fig1 (the fan of three candidates). Reusable for any generate-then-s

families.name: new:head-column-one-highlighted
families.definition: a column of identical head squares (h1 to hn) joined by dotted connectors with subscripted labels and a curly brace on one side, with one head picked out in the accent colour as the head under study. Used by iclr25-0150_fig1 (the Safety Hea

families.name: new:hierarchical-policy-stack

families.definition: a thick arrow between two stages carrying a small icon above its tail and a verb label under its shaft (Design with a robot head, Embody with a robot arm), so each hand-over is named by an action and a pictogram. Used by: iclr24-0043_fig1.

families.name: new:icon-tile-dependency-graph
families.definition: a small directed graph whose nodes are coloured icon tiles (one colour per action or object) joined by thin black arrows, under a row of layer labels (L0 to L9), with a row of tiles captioned OPEN or CLOSE and an arrow over the row naming a

families.name: new:io-pair-capsule
families.definition: a capsule split by a slanted slash into two halves in two hues carrying the letters I and O (input and output), followed by x N: stands for the sampled input-output pairs of a data set; used by icml25-0022_fig1. Reusable for any paired data

families.name: new:layer-stack-upward-arrows
families.definition: a whole model drawn as a vertical stack of identical rounded layer blocks joined by small upward arrows, coloured per model (yellow for one model, pale blue for the other). Used by acl23-0041_fig1 (Model A and Model B). Reusable for any mod

families.name: new:lettered-panel-frame
families.definition: an empty rounded grey panel with a bold title carrying a parenthesised letter ((A) Modeling Safety) set inside its top-left corner, used as one of a chain of lettered stage panels; a thick outline can mark the last stage. Used by neurips25-

families.name: new:lettered-token-circles

families.name: new:model-cascade-card

families.name: new:nested-scope-arcs

families.definition: four rings in red, gold, green and blue with a yellow title bar

families.definition: a filled circle with a white italic numeral on the left edge of a box to give its reading order. Used by: neurips25-0082_fig1. Reusable on any numbered stage list

families.definition: a small labelled chip for a hyper-parameter or ratio (a grey dashed input box feeding a blue rounded node) that sends arrows to the blocks it controls. Used by icml25-0107_fig1 (split ratio with mask ratio upper-bound feeding two selection

families.definition: light-grey framed program box with a black title tab; hole boxes with backticked natural-language text joined by data-flow arrows named by variable

families.name: new:quadrant-steps

entries.name: step-callout-cream-circled-number-on-top-edge

entries.name: aligned-timestamp-seqnum-signature-columns
entries.depicts: two tinted columns aligning three stacked labelled rows (timestamp, sequence-number range with an ellipsis run, derived signature) for the same packets; the signature cells are outlined in red to mark values referenced elsewhere

entries.name: all-to-all-fanout-triplet-solid-dashed
entries.depicts: three small multi-cell source boxes each fanning out to matching-index cells in three destination boxes above: one dashed vertical link to the same-index box, two solid diagonal links crossing to the other boxes -- a compact all-to-all exchange
entries.notes: distinct from the earlier crossbar-transfer-arrows cuts by its strict NxN same-vs-cross-box dashed/solid distinction rather than thickness=volume
entries.variant: NxN solid/dashed same-index fanout triplet

entries.name: antenna-branch-weight-multiplier-waveforms
entries.depicts: solid antenna triangle icon labelled with a subscripted signal name, feeding a red sine waveform into a circled weight-multiplier node
entries.notes: labels are rendered as outlined vector glyphs rather than <text>, so the tool reports 0 text though the labels render correctly
entries.varies: waveform phase/amplitude; weight label; subscript index

entries.name: bidirectional-arrow-chain-feedback-loop
entries.depicts: chain of 5 colour-coded module boxes joined by plain arrows, one adjacent pair also linked by a double-headed red arrow, and a long overhead arrow looping from the first box back into a later one
entries.varies: number of modules/colours; which pair gets the bidirectional arrow; loop-back target

entries.name: bipartite-crossbar-weighted-4edge

entries.varies: number of edges/labels, value shown, monochrome vs colour-coded per commodity

entries.name: bit-cell-row-alternating-colors-diamond-ends
entries.depicts: a row of individual single-bit cells coloured in alternating red/blue runs (marking which codeword each run of bits came from), bookended by a black diamond question-mark tile
entries.notes: right diamond bookend may be clipped by the bbox's right edge; left diamond and full bit pattern are intact
entries.varies: bit count/values; colour-run boundaries; end-tile glyph

entries.name: bowtie-crossbar-traffic-90pct-default
entries.depicts: two lanes (GPU0/GPU1) each split into two colour-coded branch tiles, crossing through a wide grey bowtie/hourglass shape labelled 90%, visualising heavy inter-lane traffic
entries.notes: pairs with bowtie-crossbar-traffic-narrowed-optimal (same figure, after re-placement)
entries.varies: bowtie width (= traffic amount); tile colours/labels; number of lanes

entries.name: bowtie-crossbar-traffic-narrowed-optimal
entries.depicts: same two-lane branch layout re-assigned so the bowtie crossing is drawn much narrower, showing reduced inter-lane traffic after optimal placement
entries.notes: source paper's caption states traffic drops from 90% to 10%, but the figure itself left a stale '90%' text label on both panels -- the narrower bowtie shape is the real signal, not the text; worth flagging if the merge ever surfaces part text verbatim
entries.varies: bowtie width (= traffic amount); tile colours/labels

entries.name: bracket-grouped-tile-row-labeled
entries.depicts: row of numbered colour-coded tiles grouped by a bracket and named with a single-letter category label
entries.notes: combines slot-array with brace-annotation

entries.name: capacity-labelled-triangle-topology
entries.depicts: a 3-node triangle topology with double-parallel-line edges, each labelled with a plain capacity number
entries.notes: new family new:capacity-topology-edge: double-line edge style plus a plain numeric capacity label, for network-flow/traffic-engineering topology figures. The source SVG's 'C' node label is fused into one <text> with an unrelated caption tspan ('C(a)Network traffic pattern') sharing one bbox -- tried 'include' to pull it in but that dragged the whole far-away caption text into the same cut (canvas ballooned to 217x63) which is worse than leaving it out; kept without the C label, noted here rather than spending a 3rd round
entries.varies: node count/layout, capacity values, edge line style

entries.name: capacity-topology-multi-job-overlay
entries.depicts: small network of capacity-labelled links between circle nodes, overlaid with 3 differently-styled coloured job-flow paths: a solid green arrow, a dashed blue underline, and a right-angle-turning dotted gold arrow
entries.notes: per-commodity coloured flow paths sharing one plain capacity graph, matching new:capacity-topology-edge
entries.varies: topology shape; number of overlaid flows; line style per flow

entries.name: chain-of-record-boxes-with-ellipsis
entries.depicts: chain of near-identical multi-field record boxes linked by plain arrows, with a horizontal ellipsis standing in for the omitted middle boxes and a count caption
entries.notes: new family: showing first/last of a long repeated chain of identical records with an ellipsis gap and count label, distinct from slot-array (these are multi-field record boxes, not simple cells); 224pt wide, kept since showing first+ellipsis+last is the whole point
entries.variant: chain of near-identical record boxes with an ellipsis for omitted middles
entries.varies: field names/values; count caption; number of boxes shown

entries.name: cloud-hub-multi-arrow-fanin
entries.depicts: an organic cloud-shaped hub labelled as a shared interconnect, with two colours of double-headed arrows converging on it from multiple directions, one arrow pair carrying a coloured step badge
entries.notes: new family: a cloud/blob (not circle) hub receiving multiple colour-coded bidirectional arrows -- distinct from hub-leaf-fan-node (one weighted arrow fanning to leaves) and radial-merge-node (small circle, single operator)
entries.variant: cloud hub with multi-colour bidirectional arrows converging on it
entries.varies: arrow colours/count; cloud label; badge

entries.name: cluster-oval-sink-weighted-funnel

entries.name: cluster-oval-source-weighted-fanout
entries.depicts: plain black-outline circle labelled S clustering 3 nodes (a filled blue, b/c filled grey), a fanning out to b and c via straight arrows each carrying a decimal weight label (0.33, 0.67)
entries.notes: plain outline variant of the cluster-oval-graph idiom (earlier waves' examples used a translucent fill); pairs with cluster-oval-sink-weighted-funnel from the same figure

entries.name: color-coded-parallel-port-arrows

entries.name: colour-coded-channel-processing-chain-fft

entries.notes: a second near-identical instance (Channel #2, blue) exists in the same figure, not re-cut

entries.name: colour-coded-parameter-table
entries.depicts: a two-column table (Capacity | Demand) whose demand row-keys are coloured text matching a colour-coding used elsewhere in the figure
entries.notes: companion to nsdi26-047's colour-coded-inline-legend-text -- another instance of colouring table text (not swatches) to cross-reference a diagram's colour key

entries.name: connector-style-legend-rdma-tcp-plan

entries.name: crossbar-arrows-varying-thickness-3color
